'''Kevon Grant Looney''' (born February 6, 1996) is an American [[basketball]] player. As a freshman playing [[college basketball]] with the [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA Bruins]], he earned second-team [[List of All-Pacific-12 Conference men's basketball teams|all-conference]] honors in the [[Pacific-12 Conference men's basketball|Pacific-12]], and was named to their all-freshman team in 2014–15. After the season, he decided to forego his college eligibility and enter the [[2015 NBA draft]].

Growing up in [[Wisconsin]], Looney was named the top high school player in the state as a senior in 2014. He also received national recognition as a five-star prospect and earned [[All-American]] honors. In his only season at UCLA, he led all freshmen in the nation in [[double-double]]s, recording double figures in both [[point (basketball)|points]] and [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] in 15 games. 

==Early life==
[[File:20140402 MCDAAG Kevon Looney dunk (cropped).JPG|thumb|left|upright|Looney in the [[2014 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2014 McDonald's All-American Game]]]]
Looney was born in [[Milwaukee, Wisconsin]] to Doug and Victoria Looney.<ref name=ucla_bio/> As a youngster, he watched his older brother Kevin, who was six years older, play [[pickup game]]s. Like his brother, Looney became a [[Los Angeles Lakers]] and [[Kobe Bryant]] fan, and would watch tapes of Bryant and copy the Lakers star's moves.<ref name=kartje_07252014/>

Looney was the best player on his high school team at [[Alexander Hamilton High School (Milwaukee)|Alexander Hamilton High]] in Milwaukee.<ref name=kartje_07252014>{{cite news|last=Kartje|first=Ryan|title=Versatile Looney could be a game-changer for UCLA basketball|date=July 25, 2014|newspaper=Orange County Register|url=http://www.ocregister.com/articles/looney-629872-alford-ucla.html|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6UG4jeU34|archivedate=November 21, 2014|deadurl=no}}</ref><ref name=langemo_02042014>{{cite news|last=Langemo|first=Laura|title=MPS’ Kevon Looney named McDonald’s All-American|date=February 4, 2014|work=Fox 6 News|url=http://fox6now.com/2014/02/04/mps-student-kevon-looney-named-mcdonalds-all-american/|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6UG5QEH8y|archivedate=November 21, 2014|deadurl=no}}</ref> He was already being [[recruiting (college athletics)|recruited by colleges]] as a freshman, receiving offers from in-state schools [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette]] and [[Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball|Wisconsin]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Bates|first=Greg|title=Kevon Looney draws comparisons as next Kevin Durant|date=June 8, 2012|work=Max Preps|url=http://www.maxpreps.com/news/RIHKq5V-I0WxoVrVrF1R-A/kevon-looney-draws-comparisons-as-next-kevin-durant.htm|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6UGjmA4x7|archivedate=November 22, 2014|deadurl=no}}</ref> In his sophomore year in 2012, he was named Player of the Year of the [[Milwaukee City Conference]] after averaging 20.9 [[point (basketball)|point]]s, 8.6 [[rebound (basketball)|rebound]]s and 2.0 [[assist (basketball)|assist]]s per game.<ref name=ucla_bio/><ref>{{cite news|last=Stewart|first=Mark|title=All-area capsules|date=April 4, 2012|newspaper=The Milwaukee Journal Sentinel|url=http://www.jsonline.com/sports/preps/areacaps05-vn4rj0g-146218075.html|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6UGiNSsRR|archivedate=November 22, 2014|deadurl=no}}</ref> As a junior, Looney  averaged 26.1 points, 12.4 rebounds, 7.0 [[block (basketball)|block]]s and 3.1 assists per game, and led a team of mostly unproven players to a runner-up finish for the conference title.<ref name=ucla_bio/><ref name=stewart_10312014/>

In his final season, he averaged 27.9 points, 12.7 rebounds, 7.0 assists and 8.0 blocks per game;<ref name=ucla_bio>{{cite news|title=Kevon Looney Bio|work=UCLA Bruins|url=http://www.uclabruins.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=30500&ATCLID=209575061|accessdate=November 21, 2014}}</ref> both [[CBS Sports]] and ''[[The Post-Crescent]]'' called his averages "nearly" a [[quadruple-double]].<ref name=vecenie_11152014/><ref>{{cite news|last=Arguello|first=Ricardo|title=Seymour Thunder's Sandy Cohen leads all-state team|date=March 26, 2014|newspaper=The Post-Crescent|url=http://usatodayhss.com/2014/seymour-thunders-sandy-cohen-leads-all-state-team|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6VIuFKxFc|archivedate=January 3, 2015|deadurl=no}}</ref> Though he was Hamilton's tallest player, he was also their best passer, and played mostly at [[point guard]].<ref name=kartje_07252014/><ref name=stewart_03262014/> Hamilton went undefeated in conference play to win its first league title in four years,<ref name=stewart_04102014/> and Looney earned his second City Conference player of the year award.<ref name=stewart_03262014>{{cite news|last=Stewart|first=Mark|title=Milwaukee Hamilton's Looney, Brown Deer's Appleby win state honors|date=March 26, 2014|newspaper=The Milwaukee Journal Sentinel|url=http://www.jsonline.com/sports/preps/milwaukee-hamiltons-looney-brown-deers-appleby-win-state-honors-b99233979z1-252571871.html|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6UGpc46Tm|archivedate=November 22, 2014|deadurl=no}}</ref> He gained national recognition, becoming just the second player in [[Milwaukee Public Schools]] history, and the sixth ever in Wisconsin, to be named a [[McDonald's All-American]]; he was a [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]] as well.<ref name=langemo_02042014/><ref name=stewart_03262014/> Looney was named [[Wisconsin Mr. Basketball]] by the Wisconsin Basketball Coaches Association, and [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade]] and the [[Associated Press]] named him their state player of the year.<ref name="stewart_04102014">{{cite news|last=Stewart|first=Mark|title=Hamilton's Kevon Looney not resting on laurels|date=April 10, 2014|newspaper=The Milwaukee Journal Sentinel|url=http://www.jsonline.com/sports/preps/hamiltons-kevon-looney-not-resting-on-laurels-b99245340z1-254846611.html|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6UGnt3e4J|archivedate=November 22, 2014|deadurl=no}}</ref> He was listed as a five-star prospect by [[Rivals.com]], [[ESPN.com]] and [[Scout.com]], who ranked him nationally as the No. 10, No. 12, and No. 15 player, respectively.<ref name=ucla_bio/>

==College career==
Looney announced on [[Halloween]] in 2013 his decision to attend the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] (UCLA). No recruiting analysts at [[247Sports.com]] had predicted his decision, which was a secret to everyone including his parents.<ref name=vecenie_11152014>{{cite news|last=Vecenie|first=Sam|title=UCLA freshman Kevon Looney ready to make instant impact|date=November 15, 2014|work=CBS Sports|url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/24800210/ucla-freshman-kevon-looney-ready-to-make-instant-impact|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6UG6OSoqZ|archivedate=November 21, 2014|deadurl=no}}</ref> Looney liked California, and called UCLA the "most beautiful campus I had ever seen."<ref name=stewart_10312014>{{cite news|last=Stewart|first=Mark|title=Milwaukee Hamilton basketball star Kevon Looney chooses UCLA|date=October 31, 2014|newspaper=The Milwaukee Journal Sentinel|url=http://www.jsonline.com/sports/preps/milwaukee-hamilton-basketball-star-kevon-looney-chooses-ucla-b99132349z1-230080281.html|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6UG70jvG9|archivedate=November 21, 2014|deadurl=no}}</ref> He was impressed with UCLA coach [[Steve Alford]]'s vision for the team.<ref>{{cite new|last=Hernandez|first=Rob|title=College basketball: Milwaukee Hamilton's Kevon Looney chooses UCLA over Badgers|date=November 1, 2013|work=Madison.com|url=http://host.madison.com/sports/college/basketball/men/college-basketball-milwaukee-hamilton-s-kevon-looney-chooses-ucla-over/article_d1349d56-4266-11e3-bbd7-001a4bcf887a.html|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6UG5m5Jqv|archivedate=November 21, 2014|deadurl=no}}</ref> The Bruins did not guarantee Looney a feature role as a freshman, but sold to him that he would be allowed to play both inside and outside and show his versatility, much like [[Kyle Anderson (basketball)|Kyle Anderson]] did for the Bruins in [[2013–14 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2013–14]].<ref name=kartje_07252014/>

[[File:Kevon Looney and Malik Martin.jpg|thumb|upright|Looney as a UCLA freshman on defense against [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]]]]
Playing [[power forward (basketball)|power forward]] for UCLA, Looney was one of the top freshman in the country in [[2014–15 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2014–15]].<ref name=helfand_03112015>{{cite news|last=Helfand|first=Zach|title=UCLA's Kevon Looney is on the bubble too|date=March 11, 2015|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/la-sp-ucla-looney-lakers-20150312-story.html|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6Wzc1FVN5|archivedate=March 13, 2015|deadurl=no}}</ref> In the season opener, he debuted with 20 points, nine rebounds and three assists in a 113–78 win over [[Montana State Bobcats men's basketball|Montana State]]. [[CBS Sports]] called his performance "one of the more impressive freshman debuts in UCLA's rich history."<ref name=vecenie_11152014/> He followed up with [[double-double]]s in his next four games, and became the first freshman in UCLA history with at least four double-doubles in his first five games.{{#tag:ref|Looney had earlier become the fourth UCLA freshman in the past 22 years with a double-double in either of his first two games.<ref>{{cite news|title=UCLA routs Nicholls 107-74 for 3rd straight win|date=November 20, 2014|work=ESPN|agency=Associated Press|url=http://espn.go.com/los-angeles/ncb/recap?gameId=400593197|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6UGiystzr|archivedate=November 22, 2014|deadurl=no}}</ref> The first three were [[Charles O'Bannon]], [[Kevin Love]], and [[Kyle Anderson (basketball)|Kyle Anderson]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Bonsignore|first=Vincent|title=UCLA freshman Kevon Looney is gobbling up the double-doubles|date=December 12, 2014|newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News|url=http://www.dailynews.com/sports/20141212/ucla-freshman-kevon-looney-is-gobbling-up-the-double-doubles|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20141213004024/http://www.dailynews.com/sports/20141212/ucla-freshman-kevon-looney-is-gobbling-up-the-double-doubles|archivedate=December 12, 2014|deadurl=no}}</ref> Looney later became the first Bruins freshman with two double-doubles in his first three games.<ref>{{cite web|title=Long Beach State (2-2) at UCLA (3-0)|publisher=UCLA Sports Information|url=http://www.uclabruins.com/pdf9/2994507.pdf|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6UID33JY0|archivedate=November 23, 2014|deadurl=no}}</ref>|group=lower-alpha}}<ref name=ucla_bio/> Soon, pundits began projecting Looney as a freshman [[NBA lottery pick|lottery pick]] should  he decide to enter the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA).<ref name=vecenie_11152014/><ref>{{cite news|last=Tucker|first=Kyle|title=Kentucky rolls to rout of UCLA|date=December 20, 2014|newspaper=USA Today|url=http://sports.usatoday.com/2014/12/20/kentucky-rolls-to-rout-of-ucla/|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6WzceLfBp|archivedate=March 13, 2015|deadurl=no}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Medcalf|first=Myron|title=Weekend Predictions: Kansas falls in K.C.|date=December 12, 2014|work=ESPN.com|url=http://espn.go.com/blog/collegebasketballnation/post/_/id/101409/weekend-predictions-kansas-falls-at-phog|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6Wzcs21vm|archivedate=March 13, 2015|deadurl=no}}</ref> He had seven double-doubles in the Bruins' first 10 games, before scoring in double digits just once during a five-game losing streak for UCLA, which included an 0–2 start to their [[Pacific-12 Conference men's basketball|Pacific-12 Conference]] schedule.<ref>{{cite news|last=Kartje|first=Ryan|title=Alford searching for right buttons to turn around Bruins|date=January 6, 2015|newspaper=Orange County Register|url=http://www.ocregister.com/articles/ucla-647318-alford-looney.html|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6VTIuJUQn|archivedate=January 10, 2015|deadurl=no}}</ref> Looney helped the team end their streak with career highs of 27 points and 19 rebounds in a 86–81 double-[[overtime (sports)|overtime]] win over [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Helfand|first=Zach|title=UCLA ends losing streak with 86-81, double-overtime win over Stanford|date=January 8, 2015|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/la-sp-ucla-stanford-20150109-story.html|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6VTJCLtf4|archivedate=January 10, 2015|deadurl=no}}</ref><ref>{{cite Sports|url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/24947676/kevon-looneys-night-leaves-nba-scouts-drooling-gives-ucla-hope|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6VTB0Upur|archivedate=January 10, 2015|deadurl=no}}</ref> He was one of 14 players named to the midseason watch list of the [[United States Basketball Writers Association]] (USBWA) for the [[Wayman Tisdale Award]], presented annually to the nation's top freshman.<ref>{{cite web|title=UCLA's Kevon Looney Named to Wayman Tisdale Award Midseason List|date=January 23, 2015|work=UCLA Bruins|url=http://www.uclabruins.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=30500&ATCLID=209861730|accessdate=January 26, 2015}}</ref> He was also one of 16 finalists for the inaugural [[Karl Malone Award]], given to the top power forward in [[Division I (NCAA)|Division I]] men's basketball.<ref>{{cite news|title=Wyoming's Nance finalist for Karl Malone Award|date=February 17, 2015|newspaper=USA Today|agency=Associated Press|url=http://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2015/02/17/wyomings-nance-finalist-for-karl-malone-award/23552191/|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6WzeGddUp|archivedate=March 13, 2015|deadurl=no}}</ref> 

UCLA rarely called plays for Looney, and his scoring typically came off putbacks, fast breaks, and open shots.<ref name=wang_03182015>{{cite news|last=Wang|first=Jack|title=Kevon Looney’s UCLA career could end with unfulfilled promise|date=March 18, 2015|newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News|url=http://www.dailynews.com/sports/20150318/kevon-looneys-ucla-career-could-end-with-unfulfilled-promise|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6X8dZu1k6|archivedate=March 19, 2015|deadurl=no}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Wang|first=Jack|title=Can UCLA’s Kevon Looney be more than a ‘garbage guy’?|date=January 10, 2015|newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News|url=http://www.dailynews.com/sports/20150130/can-uclas-kevon-looney-be-more-than-a-garbage-guy|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6X8dh5Ovq|archivedate=March 19, 2015|deadurl=no}}</ref> A natural at rebounding, his shooting improved as the season progressed. After making just nine of 28  of his [[three-point field goal]]s in the first 24 games, Looney was 11 of 17 in the last seven games of the regular season.<ref name=helfand_03112015/> Still his scoring tapered off, with only one game over 15 points since his career-game at Stanford.<ref name=wang_03182015/> In the [[2015 Pacific-12 Conference Men's Basketball Tournament|2015 Pac-12 Tournament]], Looney exited mid-game after he took an arm to his left cheek during UCLA's quarterfinal win over [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]].  He was a game-time decision to play the following day against [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]], when he was cleared and fitted with a protective mask just 90 minutes before the contest. Though impaired by the mask, he played 30 minutes but was limited, finishing below his season averages with only five points and four rebounds.<ref>{{cite news|last=Helfand|first=Zach|title=UCLA Bruins' Kevon Looney knows he faces a tough challenge|date=March 16, 2015|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/la-sp-ucla-basketball-kevon-looney-20150317-story.html|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6X88nLc4U|archivedate=March 18, 2015|deadurl=no}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Kartje|first=Ryan|title=New mask is a clear winner for UCLA's Looney|date=March 17, 2015|newspaper=Orange County Register|url=http://www.ocregister.com/articles/ucla-654574-looney-mask.html|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6X88uwENX|archivedate=March 18, 2015|deadurl=no}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Kartje|first=Ryan|title=Looney's status uncertain after facial injury|date=March 12, 2015|newspaper=Orange County Register|url=http://www.ocregister.com/ucla/looney-654051-status-midway.html|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6X89462mu|archivedate=March 18, 2015|deadurl=no}}</ref> The Bruins lost 70–64, but the close match helped them secure a bid into the [[2015 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2015 NCAA tournament]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Larry Eustachy: Players devastated|date=March 15, 2015|work=ESPN.com|url=http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/tournament/2015/story/_/id/12491646/colorado-state-temple-murray-state-snubbed-ncaa-tournament-selection-committee|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6X440wXYx|archivedate=March 16, 2015|deadurl=no}}</ref> Looney continued to play wearing the mask as UCLA advanced to the Sweet 16 for the second straight season.<ref name=dailynews_04062015/>

For the season, Looney averaged 11.6 points and led the team with 9.2 rebounds per game; he finished with 15 double-doubles. Among all freshmen nationally, his double-doubles led the nation and his rebounding ranked second.<ref>{{cite news|title=UCLA freshman Kevon Looney to leave early for NBA draft|date=April 6, 2015|newspaper=The Washington Post|agency=Associated Press|url=http://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/colleges/ucla-freshman-kevon-looney-to-leave-early-for-nba-draft/2015/04/06/2a007aa6-dca1-11e4-b6d7-b9bc8acf16f7_story.html|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6Xb8e5tZf|archivedate=March 6, 2015|deadurl=no}}</ref> His rebounds and double-doubles ranked second among all players in the Pac-12. Looney made 47.0 percent of his [[field goal (basketball)|field goals]], and 41.5 percent from three-point range.<ref name=dailynews_04062015>{{cite news|last=Wang|first=Jack|title=Kevon Looney leaving UCLA for NBA draft|date=April 6, 2015|newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News|url=http://www.dailynews.com/sports/20150406/kevon-looney-leaving-ucla-for-nba-draft|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6XbWIfox1|archivedate=April 7, 2015|deadurl=no}}</ref> He was voted second-team [[List of All-Pacific-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]], and named to the Pac-12 All-Freshman Team.<ref>{{cite press release|title=2014-15 Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Honors|date=March 9, 2015|publisher=Pac-12|url=http://pac-12.com/article/2015/03/09/2014-15-pac-12-conference-mens-basketball-honors|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6WuCA8C5K|archivedate=March 9, 2015|deadurl=no}}</ref> He was also named second-team all-district by the [[National Association of Basketball Coaches]] (NABC).<ref>{{cite press release|title=National Association of Basketball Coaches Announces 2014-15 Division I All-District Teams and UPS All-District Coaches|date=March 27, 2015|publisher=National Association of Basketball Coaches|url=http://static.psbin.com/w/9/2qxdhr73x7aqb1/2014-15_NABC_Division_I_All-District_Teams_and_Coaches-2.pdf|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6XTS4w79H|archivedate=April 1, 2015|deadurl=no}}</ref> After the season, he decided to forego his remaining college eligibility to [[NBA draft declaration|declare]] for the [[2015 NBA draft]].<ref name=dailynews_04062015/>
